content: Russians cast ballots to choose lawmakers for the State Duma, with the more-than-4 ½-year-old war on Ukraine and a slowing economy looming over the country’s first parliamentary elections since the 2022 invasion.

title: US Envoy Coale Sees Belarus Moving Toward 'Family Of Nations"

title: Billions Go Missing From Iran's Secret Oil Cash Network
content: Billions of dollars in oil revenue are missing from Iran’s coffers. At the center of the scandal are shadowy middlemen known as "trustees" who help Tehran sell oil, steel, petrochemicals, and other goods abroad while bypassing international sanctions.

title: Russian Military Airfield, Major Oil Refinery Targeted In Massive Ukrainian Drone Attack

title: Women, Life, Freedom Leaves Its Mark On A New Wave Of Iranian Cinema
content: Iranian cinema has a long history of confronting censorship. But the Women, Life, Freedom protests changed the terms of that confrontation. Where filmmakers once worked within, or carefully around, an elaborate approval system to tell their stories, many now bypass it entirely at great risk.

title: Russian Drones Hit Ukrainian Passenger Train And Bus, Killing 5
content: Russian drones hit a passenger train in southern Ukraine on September 16, setting a train ablaze. No causalities were reported. Another Russian drone strike killed five people on a bus near Nikopol, according to officials. The strikes follow an uptick in attacks on civilian transport in recent days.

title: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci Sentenced To 25 Years For War Crimes
content: The 58-year-old Thaci, and three other former leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army who fought Serb forces in the 1998-99 war, was convicted on four counts of war crimes: illegal and arbitrary arrest and detention, cruel treatment, torture, and murder.
